paper.title_en: Constraints on Schwarzschild Black Hole in a Generalized Dehnen-Type $(1,4,γ)$ Dark Matter Halo via the S2 Star Orbit around Sgr A$^\star$
paper.abstract_en: The distribution of dark matter (DM) halo around supermassive black holes (BHs) may leave observable imprints on stellar dynamics near galactic centers. Motivated by this, we investigate the orbital motion of the S2 star in the spacetime of a recently derived generalized Schwarzschild BH solution embedded in a Dehnen-type $(1,4,γ)$ DM halo, considering it as a possible model for Sgr A$^{\star}$ at the center of the Milky Way. Unlike previous studies restricted to specific values of the halo parameter $γ$, the present solution describes the fully generalized case with arbitrary $γ$. We derive the corresponding equations of motion and obtain the associated pericenter shift over one orbital period. Using observational data of the S2 star, we constrain the parameters of the Schwarzschild--Dehnen BH-DM system through a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis. Our MCMC analysis provides constraints on the parameter $γ$ of the generalized Dehnen-type DM halo. The posterior medians of $γ$ with 68% credible intervals are $γ=0.652^{+0.435}_{-0.446}$ and $γ=0.771^{+0.486}_{-0.522}$ for Dataset 1 from Do et al. and Dataset 2 from Gillessen et al., respectively. The corresponding one-sided 95% upper credible limits are $γ<1.238$ and $γ<1.389$. If the halo is instead normalized to the observed local dark-matter density at solar distance, $ρ_{\rm DM}(8\,\mathrm{kpc})\simeq0.01\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{pc}^{-3}$, the 95% upper limits become $γ<1.949$ and $γ<1.931$ for Dataset 1 and Dataset 2, respectively. The analysis shows that the S2 orbital motion provides constraints on the parameter $γ$ of the DM halo profile, while the characteristic halo density $ρ_s$ and scale radius $r_s$ exhibit a strong degeneracy and remain sensitive to the adopted prior ranges.
